sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Clarksville?
sections.html:
A house inside Clarksville is taxed twice, by the county and by the city, and each payment has its own destination. The Montgomery County Assessor of Property sets values. The Montgomery County Trustee takes the county share, and the city's Finance and Revenue Department takes the city share.

  • Montgomery County Trustee: 350 Pageant Lane, Suite 101-B, (931) 648-5717. Weekday hours run from 7:30 in the morning to 4:30, with extra Saturday mornings in February until noon.
  • Montgomery County Assessor of Property: 350 Pageant Lane, Suite 101-C, (931) 648-5709. Go here for name or address corrections and classification questions.
  • City Finance and Revenue: One Public Square, Suite 119, or the North Clarksville Service Center at 111 Cunningham Lane. Call (931) 645-7436 between 8 and 4:30 on weekdays.

Nothing the Trustee collects covers the city. Outside the city limits, a house owes only the county.

Montgomery County levies $2.10 for 2026 and the city adds $1.01, both counted per $100 of assessed value. That is $3.11 combined for a city address. The County Commission and City Council vote on rates in July, so any estimate made before then is built on the earlier year.

For a rough bill, convert the appraisal to an assessed value at 25 percent, then apply 3.11 percent to the result. Rounding on the real bill can move the total by a few dollars. The county Assessor's site also has a proration calculator for splitting a year between buyer and seller.

You can start paying on the first Monday of October. No interest accrues until the final day of February closes. Come March 1, the balance is delinquent and 1.5 percent is added monthly, a rate the county calls 18 percent a year.

Statements from the county are mailed the last week of October, and the city sends its own during October. You may make partial payments on the county bill from July 10 as long as the full amount is in by the February deadline, though online county payments must be for the whole balance. Billing follows ownership on January 1. After a later sale, the notice may still carry the previous owner's name.

City tax that stays delinquent for a year goes to the delinquent tax attorney. From then on the Clerk and Master of Montgomery Chancery Court takes the payment at 2 Millennium Plaza, Number 101, (931) 648-5703.

sections.h2: How do you pay a Clarksville property tax bill?
sections.html:
County and city bills are paid separately, because each office accepts only its own.

  • County online: an e-check adds 1.75 percent plus $1.00, while Visa or Mastercard adds 2.65 percent plus $1.00.
  • County by mail or drop box: the 24 hour drop box outside the Trustee's office accepts checks, cashier's checks and money orders, not cash.
  • County at banks: F and M Bank, Planters Bank, Cumberland Bank and Trust, and United Community Bank take full payments through February 28, 2027, if you bring the original bill.
  • City: online with a 2.5 percent processor fee, by mail to P.O. Box 30549 in Clarksville, or at the Revenue Office or the drop box left of City Hall's main doors.

The city refunds an overpayment to whoever paid second. When a mortgage servicer pays in December and the owner also pays in February, the refund goes to the servicer first.

Two state programs can lower the burden for qualifying owners. Tax Relief refunds part of the tax to elderly and disabled owners, and to disabled veteran owners and surviving spouses. Tax Freeze holds the bill at the figure from the first qualifying year.

Tax Relief forms are available at the Trustee's office and at city Finance and Revenue, and a first-time applicant only needs to sign up at one. Tax Freeze enrollment happens at the county Trustee, which passes the news to the city. Recipients send in a voucher every year to both the county and the city, because the state uses those vouchers to repay the covered share. For the city side, call (931) 645-7436.

Leaving taxes unpaid for years can end with your house sold at public auction. Montgomery County offers parcels at least two years behind at its tax sale, held at the Montgomery County Courts Center, 2 Millennium Plaza.

Chancery Court orders the sale for cash. Afterward the former owner, a lien holder or heirs get one year to buy it back by paying taxes, interest, penalties and costs, and interest on the redemption price can run up to 10 percent a year. Only state and federal liens survive the sale. The city adds that the house can be auctioned no matter who was supposed to pay under a private contract, so a buyer's promise to pay protects nothing.

Clarksville is the only incorporated city in Montgomery County and sits next to Fort Campbell. Its population was 166,722 in 2020 and an estimated 188,829 in July 2025. Survey data for 2020 to 2024 show 67,832 households and a median rent of $1,307. Roughly 55.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied, which leaves many rentals in the mix.

sections.h2: How taxes work when you sell a Clarksville house
sections.html:
New owners are directed to the closing statement to see who pays for the year of transfer. Whatever is unpaid remains on the property itself. A closing agent can request payoffs from the Trustee and the city and settle both out of the sale proceeds.

Ask for a calculation of the share of the calendar year each side owns the house. The county Assessor posts a proration calculator that splits the year at a date you choose, which gives you a starting number to compare with the closing statement.

For a seller who wants a fast closing, a short checklist helps:

  • Get a payoff from the county Trustee and another from city Finance and Revenue.
  • Confirm that no relief or freeze voucher is outstanding for the year.
  • Ask the title company to add both payoffs to the settlement statement.
  • Keep the original bills in case a bank or office asks for them.

faqs.q: What is the Clarksville property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: Montgomery County charges $2.10 and the city charges $1.01 for 2026, each per $100 of assessed value. Inside Clarksville that adds up to $3.11 per $100, applied to 25 percent of the appraised value.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Clarksville city property tax?
faqs.a: Walk in to Finance and Revenue at One Public Square, Suite 119, or the North Clarksville Service Center on Cunningham Lane. Mail to P.O. Box 30549 also works, as does the online portal with its 2.5 percent fee.

faqs.q: Do I pay the Montgomery County Trustee and the city separately?
faqs.a: Yes, two bills mean two payments. The Trustee handles the county portion and the city handles its own portion for any house inside Clarksville.

faqs.q: How long before Clarksville can sell a house for unpaid tax?
faqs.a: A parcel two or more years delinquent can be put up at the Montgomery County tax sale. The owner then gets a one year redemption period.

faqs.q: Who can I call about my Clarksville assessment?
faqs.a: The Montgomery County Assessor of Property answers at (931) 648-5709. A formal appeal is heard by the county Board of Equalization, usually starting June 1. Ask the Assessor for the filing cutoff.
